nodes.text: Chapter 20: Current, Resistance, Ohm's Law, Power, AC/DC

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Hand-drawn circuit consisting of a rectangular wire loop and a battery on the left. The battery is labeled V, with a positive terminal at the top and a negative terminal at the bottom. Blue arrows labeled I show conventional current moving clockwise: rightward across the top, downward on the right, and leftward across the bottom. Black arrows and e⁻ labels show electrons moving in the opposite direction around the loop.
nodes.figure_alternative: Circuit diagram contrasting clockwise conventional current with oppositely directed electron flow.

nodes.text: Electrical current (I) is the rate of flow of positive charge.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: I equals Q divided by delta t, which equals Q divided by t.

nodes.text: It's direction (from DC, or direct current, voltage) is opposite the ‘flow’ of electrons: from + to −.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: Open bracket A close bracket equals C divided by s.

nodes.text: Electric fields in a Simple Circuit (1962)

nodes.detailed_figure_description: Annotated grayscale photograph of a simple circuit or conductor arrangement with two connections entering from above. Field patterns appear around and within the conducting region. A left callout points into the conductor and reads, “Internal electric field: constant magnitude and parallel to the axis of the conductor.” A right callout points outside the conductor and reads, “External electric field: Produced by the surface charges.”
nodes.figure_alternative: Annotated photograph distinguishing the internal electric field in a conductor from the external field produced by surface charges.

warnings.message: The source reads “It's direction,” apparently using “It's” where the possessive “Its” may have been intended.
